title: interactive-callgraph-connectors-notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad exploring a lightweight, interactive callgraph API and connector pattern for live LLM inference traces. Goal is fast dev/debug workflows (local dev + staging) and a path to production-safe telemetry with low overhead.

Summary idea:
- Add an optional per-request "callgraph session" that emits structured events (node enter/exit, KV cache hits, kernel selection, fallback routing decisions).
- Events stream to one or more connectors: local file, in-memory UI, OTLP collector, or a small web UI that can render a callgraph and time-series.
- Callgraph sessions are opt-in via request header or SDK flag; sampling + redact rules applied.

Non-goals (for now): full distributed tracing replacement, PII-aware archival policies (we can add later).

High-level flow diagram (ASCII):

  Client SDK ---(generate)-> Ingress Proxy ---+---> Serving Router ---> Worker (GPU)
                                              |
                                              +---> Callgraph-sink (local/inproc/otlp)

Events: minimal, typed, append-only stream per session. Keep small schema.

Event model (flat fields only; example event as JSON string):
{"timestamp":"2024-09-18T14:23:05.123Z","session_id":"cg-7f9a","seq":12,"event_type":"kernel_select","node_id":"n19","payload":"fp16-kernel-v3","duration_ms":1.2}",

Notes on schema decisions:
- Use flat key/value pairs for easy index/search in logs/OTLP.
- event_type enum: start, end, op_enter, op_exit, cache_hit, cache_miss, kernel_select, fallback, external_call, error, metric
- node_id is opaque string to represent logical node (e.g., token-step, attention-op).
- seq monotonic within session to simplify reordering concerns.

API shapes (HTTP) -- prototype paths:
1) Start session (id returned, server may sample/drop):
POST /v1/debug/callgraph/start
Headers: Authorization, X-Redwood-Callgraph: sampling=high;redact=partial
Body: {"request_id":"r-123","intent":"dev-debug","max_events":1000}
Response: {"session_id":"cg-7f9a","accepted":true,"policy":"sampled"}

2) Emit event (best-effort, 202 accepted):
POST /v1/debug/callgraph/event
Headers: Authorization, X-Callgraph-Session: cg-7f9a
Body: {"timestamp":"...","seq":1,"event_type":"op_enter","node_id":"n1","meta":"tokenize()","duration_ms":0}
Server side validates schema, maybe enriches with host/runtime-id, and forwards to configured sinks.

3) Export/flush session for post-mortem:
GET /v1/debug/callgraph/export?session_id=cg-7f9a&format=graphml,jsonl
-> returns compiled events or pre-rendered graph.

Config sketch (runtime config -- YAML style, prototyping):
callgraph:
  enabled: true
  global_sampling_rate: 0.01
  max_events_per_session: 2000
  sinks:
    - type: file
      path: /var/log/redwood/callgraphs/%Y%m%d/%session_id%.jsonl
      rotate: daily
    - type: otlp
      endpoint: https://otel-collector.prod:4317
      batch_size: 512
      insecure: false
  redact_rules:
    - path_regex: ".*user_input.*"
      method: mask
      mask_with: "[REDACTED]"

Connector pattern notes:
- Implement small adapter interface: start(session), emit(event), close(session). Keep sync call cheap; emit uses background batching.
- Connectors should be cancellable when memory pressure or high load.
- Local-dev connector: in-memory circular buffer + mini-web UI that can step through seqs.
- Staging/prod connectors: OTLP + S3 export for offline repros.

UI sketch (quick):
- Graph pane (left): nodes with durations (width ~ duration). Hover shows meta.
- Timeline (bottom): stacked lanes (kernel, cache, routing).
- Event list (right): raw JSON events with copy button and redaction indicators.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Overhead: we must ensure events are cheap (few hundred bytes). Allow server-side sampling to completely drop heavy sessions.
- Privacy: must integrate redact rules early. Consider u-turn where callgraph events with user input are only kept in ephemeral tracing bucket and never persisted to long-term storage.
- Multi-worker sessions: session_id must be globally unique and include shard hints to reduce collision. Events may arrive out-of-order; seq solves reordering locally but cross-worker clocks need caution.
- Backpressure: If sink is slow, should runtime drop events or block request? Prefer drop w/ counters emitted to metrics.
- Security: session token in header should be short-lived and scoped to debugging role.

Prototype implementation plan (short):
- Week 0: implement in-memory connector + /start /event endpoints (dev build). Add SDK flag to opt-in.
- Week 1: add basic web UI that reads inproc buffer (ws).
- Week 2: OTLP connector + simple file export. Add redact rule engine (naive).
- Week 3: add sampling policy support and metric dashboards for dropped events.

Small examples (SDK usage snippets):
Python pseudocode:
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., callgraph_sampling=0.2)
with client.callgraph_session(intent='debug:tokenization') as cg:
    resp = client.generate(prompt)
    # SDK auto emits events: tokenization, model_call, kv_cache, kernel_select

cURL start session example:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/callgraph/start -H 'Authorization: Bearer X' -d '{"request_id":"r-1","intent":"dev"}'

Edge cases to capture in engineering doc later:
- When callgraph size exceeds max_events_per_session -> server should write a truncated marker event and stop accepting further events for that session.
- Session lifetime: TTL of 60s after last event before export/close.
- Relationship with existing tracing: provide adapters to join callgraph session id with existing trace_id for correlation.

Local TODOs (me):
- [ ] Add compact binary wire format proposal (proto vs jsonl) and cost measurements.
- [ ] Mock-up web UI screens (Figma quick).
- [ ] Run a tiny perf test on dev infra (10k requests with cg enabled at 1%).
- [ ] Write a small RFC draft for security & redact rules.

References & related threads:
- Slack: #runtime-tracing 2024-09-20 (Diego had perf numbers)
- GH PR: runtime/pull/812 (initial sink interface)
- OBS-342: user story for callgraph export to S3

Notes-to-self style endings:
- Keep event schema intentionally small; prefer many small events over fewer large nested payloads.
- This is valuable for debugging kernel/quantization regressions and ephemeral fallback causes.
- Might be useful to expose a cheap "mini-stats" header for prod: X-Callgraph-Sampled: true/false so clients can optionally attach telemetry.

If this looks promising I can convert into a formal RFC and place under shared_drives/engineering/observability/ next iteration.
